column1: # OWASP ZAP baseline scan rule thresholds (issue #785)
# Format: <rule id>
# All three columns are required (tab separated); use ".*" to apply a
# threshold to every URL.
# Reference: https://www.zaproxy.org/docs/docker/baseline-scan/
# Anything not listed here uses ZAP's default threshold (WARN). Entries here
# either silence a known false positive or explicitly escalate a category we
# want to always fail the build on. See docs/SECURITY_SCANNING_RUNBOOK.md for
# the triage process before adding new IGNORE rules.
# Retest cookie flags on /health and /metrics only after confirming they
# carry no session state — these are unauthenticated, stateless endpoints.
# Server header / X-Powered-By disclosure is already stripped by helmet in
# production; the informational finding on the dev/CI server is expected.
# --- security.yml DAST job (isolated target at 127.0.0.1:5050) ---------------
# That job scans a throwaway Express app that only implements /, /health and
# /echo. ZAP's spider still requests /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml, which fall
# through to Express' default 404 page. The three findings below describe that
# error response (no Permissions-Policy / Cache-Control on a non-existent path,
# CSP partially applied), not an application endpoint, so they are ignored for
# this target only. Scoped by host:port so the production scan in deploy.yml
# (localhost:5001) keeps flagging them.
# Always fail the build on reflected/stored XSS and SQL injection findings,
# regardless of the default threshold.
